q2_gaps: A calendar-coincidence predication whose subject is a date ('Day 0 of Year 1 fell on the autumn equinox'): the light-verb rule covers 'occurred / happened / took place' over event-nouns, but nothing says whether 'fall on <date>' reifies an ordinary event or, like a light verb, hangs the time straight on the date entity.

An entity witness in the Time slot: Time's licensed fillers are structured calendar terms, deictic/named-time constants and day-part symbols, so a named recurring occasion that must also be a referable entity ('the autumn equinox', Agent of the next clause) has no specified Time encoding.

A plural capitalized name is not addressed for the non-label case; here it does not bite, but the same rules that give 'the Wrens' a Name-only individual give no guidance on GroupOf for a multi-word plural place name.
notes: Sentence 2 ('The autumn equinox begins moth-season') is encoded as the sentence-1 witness plus an untensed (generic-default) event, which is what the definite-singular-is-a-witness rule mandates even though the clause reads as a kind-level generic. The attachment of 'near the harbor' (station vs. the Cliff Path) is a live ambiguity resolved silently, defensibly under the world-knowledge-lean rule.
